title: "Bar Plots"

```{r}
#| include: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
data("penguins")
```

[Home](../index.qmd) \> [ggplot](../ggplot.qmd) \> Bar Graphs

## Normal Bar Plot

A bar plot can be used to represent the count of one categorical variable

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = island)) +
  geom_bar()
```

You can add a fill to represent a second categorical variable

```{r}
#| warning: false
ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = island, fill = species)) +
  geom_bar()
```

## Dodged Bar Plot

A dodged Bar Plot can be used to represent two categorical variables

```{r}
#| warning: false
ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = island, fill = species)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge")
```

## Standardized Bar Plot

A standardized bar plot can be used to represent two categorical variables, but it shows only the proportions of the fill variable within the x variable

```{r}
#| warning: false
ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = island, fill = species)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill")
```
